resources.string: Enter the server address, e.g. https://meet.example.com
The server address must start with https://
Runs the installer over the server again: a new version, or a repair for one that has stopped. Rooms, invite links and the operator password are kept.

Reinstall on %1$s?

Certificate: %2$s
Room: %3$s
Port: %4$s

Rooms, invite links and the operator password are kept.
Filled in with what this server was installed with. Changing it changes the server.
Deletes the server completely, then installs it as if the machine were new. Rooms, invite links and certificates are lost, and the operator gets a new password.
Everything SOZVON holds on %1$s will be deleted, then it will be installed from scratch. Rooms, invite links and the operator password will not survive. Continue?
Removes SOZVON from the machine over SSH. Nothing else on the server is touched.
The service is stopped and removed; rooms, operator accounts, invite links and certificates stay on disk, so installing again picks them back up.
Everything goes, including rooms, operator accounts, invite links, certificates and recordings. Nothing is backed up.
Remove SOZVON from %1$s? Its rooms and accounts stay on disk.
Delete SOZVON from %1$s along with every room, operator account, invite link and certificate? This cannot be undone.
The server is removed. Its data is still on the machine — installing again will pick it up.
The server and all of its data are gone.
You are in a call. Leave it and go back to the server list?
No server yet? Set one up on your VPS
SOZVON will be installed on your VPS over SSH. You need a clean Debian or Ubuntu server and root access.
Used only during the install and never saved.
Paste the contents of the key file.
Its A record must already point at this server.
Usually takes 2–5 minutes. The install runs on the server by itself: if the connection drops, the app reconnects and keeps watching.
Write the password down — it is shown only once.
The certificate is self-signed: an ordinary browser will refuse this address, only the app will work.
The name is derived from the server\'s IP via sslip.io and the certificate comes from Let\'s Encrypt. Nothing to configure, works in any browser.
The most self-contained option: your own name, no third party in the chain.
Needs neither a domain nor access to Let\'s Encrypt. But browsers will reject such a certificate — only the app will be able to connect.
You are connecting to %1$s for the first time.
The key of server %1$s has changed since last time.
Compare it with what your hosting control panel shows. If it does not match, someone may be impersonating your server — and you are about to give them the root password.
Waiting for the server to answer
Leave empty for 443. A different port is needed when something else already uses 443 — but Let\'s Encrypt only works on 443, so pair it with a self-signed certificate.
Leave empty to download from GitHub. Set it when the server cannot reach GitHub.
Install the copy bundled with this app (%1$s)
Install the copy bundled with this app
Sends the server from your phone instead of asking it to download one. Works where GitHub is blocked. Uncheck to fetch the newest release instead.
This server\'s certificate is not trusted. Only a server installed from this app with a self-signed certificate can be opened this way.
The server\'s certificate has changed since it was installed. The connection was refused.
